pages.text: News details | FAO in Cambodia | Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Share Close Cambodia Unlocking New Opportunities for Cambodia's Mango Sector 27/07/2026 , Cambodia Growing high-quality mangoes is important, but farmers can earn more when they have access to processing, reliable buyers, and markets that value their products. Understanding what investors, processors, and consumers need is an important step toward creating more opportunities for farming communities. As Cambodia diversifies its agrifood systems beyond rice, mango has emerged as one of the country's most promising agricultural products. Between 2016 and 2020, the area under mango cultivation expanded from around 5,000 hectares to approximately 138,000 hectares, with production reaching an estimated 1.5 million tonnes. Today, mango is Cambodia's priority product under FAO's One Country One Priority Product (OCOP) initiative, reflecting its strong economic potential and cultural significance. From 24 to 26 July 2026, Mr. Gao Aiping, Professor and Mango Production Expert, and Mr. Liu Haiqing, Professor and Mango Value Chain Development Expert, from the Tropical Crops Genetic Resources Institute of the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences, visited Kampong Speu, Battambang, and Oddar Meanchey under the FAO-China South-South Cooperation Programme. pages.text: News | One Country One Priority Product (OCOP) | Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Share Close One Country One Priority Product (OCOP) News OCOP drives strong global progress in first half of 2026, gears up for key events Group photo of the OCOP Secretariat members at FAO headquarters. ©FAO/Francisco Martinez 22/07/2026 The One Country One Priority Product (OCOP) Secretariat gathered at FAO headquarters to take stock of what the initiative has delivered for farmers and national value chains over the first half of the year, while mapping out a practical course for the months ahead and into 2027. The first six months of 2026 saw steady expansion across the field, with activities spanning multiple global projects. A significant part of this work was driven by a global project under the FAO-China South–South Cooperation Programme, generously supported by the Government of China. United States Department of Transportation In This Section Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) The Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) was a large-scale FAA initiative to modernize the U.S. National Airspace System (NAS). Through NextGen, the FAA revamped air traffic control infrastructure for communications, navigation, surveillance, automation, and information management to increase the safety, efficiency, capacity, predictability, flexibility, and resiliency of U.S. aviation. NextGen’s scope included airport infrastructure improvements, new air traffic technologies and procedures, and safety and security enhancements. We engaged with the public and shared practices with the aviation community to accelerate the adoption of innovative technologies. Our modernization initiative enabled a more flexible — yet robust and resilient — aerospace infrastructure that ensures the safe introduction of non-traditional aviation, such as commercial space transportation and advanced air mobility. This allows quality values to be tightly defined and then numerically calibrated, which in turn allows for the standardization needed to support a worldwide deployment of fingerprint sensors with universally interpretable image qualities. NFIQ 2 quality features are formally standardized as part of ISO/IEC 29794-4 and serve as the reference implementation of the standard. pages.text: NG Stories | Past exhibitions | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Past exhibition NG Stories: Making a National Gallery 4 October 2024 - 12 January 2025 Admission free Gallery B Immerse yourself in 200 years of extraordinary National Gallery stories. From a resident family of 14 and an intrepid travelling agent to ground-breaking scientists and a wartime pianist, NG Stories tells the history of the National Gallery through the people who made us what we are today. There’s a slate mine in Wales where paintings were safely stored during the Second World War. A guard dog who became a member of staff. And a Keeper’s family, with 14 children, who lived in the building and kept diaries. You’ll discover some of the untold personal stories of the Gallery and the special memories we have been privileged to help create for our visitors. From childhood adventures to life-changing first art encounters, our visitors have always been at the heart of what we do. Through magical soundscapes and immersive digital interactions, you'll experience the work of the many people here at the Gallery who help to care for the paintings and see how this work has changed over the years. This experience, both online and in the Gallery, uses digital technology to tell you the unexpected human stories which have shaped the past and present of our 200-year history. pages.text: Nicaragua | International Labour Organization Ir al contenido principal Portal de país Nicaragua Facebook X Linkedin © OIT Better Work Índice de contenidos Nicaragua Cerrar Nicaragua ha sido miembro de la OIT de 1919 a 1938 y desde 1957 hasta la fecha. Ha ratificado ocho de los 10 convenios fundamentales, dos de los cuatro convenios de gobernanza y 52 convenios técnicos. Nicaragua es uno de los países más grandes de América Central, con una extensión territorial de 130 373,47 km² y cuenta con una población total de 7 046 300 habitantes (CEPALSTAT, 2023). La capital de Nicaragua es Managua, pero también destacan varias ciudades importantes como León, Granada, Masaya, Rivas y Estelí. El país se divide en 15 departamentos, dos regiones autónomas y 153 municipios. La asistencia técnica que brinda la OIT a sus constituyentes –gobierno, empleadores y trabajadores– en el país se da por medio de un equipo de especialistas y mediante la ejecución de proyectos de cooperación técnica que atienden los retos prioritarios identificados en las diferentes áreas del ámbito laboral; con el fin de cumplir con el mandato de promover el trabajo decente e impulsar la justicia social. Las acciones de la OIT en Nicaragua se coordinan desde la Oficina de la OIT para América Central, Haití, Panamá y República Dominicana . Close nicofr77's Diary À portée de train : une carte des boucles vélo accessibles en train, depuis 60 villes Posted by nicofr77 on 2 October 2026 in French (Français) . Last updated on 4 October 2026. Je publie sur Tisseur de Voies, le site où je calcule des boucles vélo avec retour en train, une carte qui répond à une question simple : depuis ma ville, jusqu’où puis-je partir à vélo en prenant un seul train ? On choisit une ville parmi 60 et une durée de train aller, de 0 à 4 heures. La carte montre en rose les véloroutes des boucles qu’on peut rejoindre, et en bleu les gares atteintes, plus foncées quand elles sont proches. Ici, Paris avec une heure de train : 1 763 boucles, contre 323 qui partent des gares parisiennes. Une boucle, c’est un itinéraire à vélo d’une gare à une autre sur des véloroutes balisées, avec un train pour rentrer. Elle compte dès qu’un train aller atteint l’une de ses gares dans la durée choisie. Un classement des 60 villes accompagne la carte : Paris, Strasbourg et Lille en tête, Brest et Quimper en queue. Les véloroutes viennent d’OpenStreetMap et du référentiel national des véloroutes, le fond de carte d’OpenStreetMap. Les durées sortent des horaires publiés en open data par la SNCF, Île-de-France Mobilités, la Région Sud et les Chemins de fer de la Corse : pour chaque trajet, la durée médiane de la ligne la plus rapide qui circule au moins une fois par jour. Seuls les trains sans changement comptent.

pages.text: Nicolas Chalumeau: a Memorial | Apache Software Foundation Nicolas Chalumeau: a Memorial Our friend Nicolas Chalumeau has departed this world on the 4th of October 2005, at the age of 27. The Apache Software Foundation would like to express its condolences to Nicolas' family and friends. Nicolas had been developing open source software at Apache for several years. He was participating in several projects, including Jakarta Cactus and Apache Maven. But even more importantly than helping those projects, what made Nicolas stand apart was his kindness and his generosity. He was always open to discussion and was constantly helping others. On the Cactus project he was regularly the first to answer questions from newcomers trying to use Cactus. Recently he had taken up the important task of helping migrate Cactus to use Cargo and he had been working diligently towards that goal. Actually Nicolas had been doing such a great job on the Cactus project that the Cactus committers had unanimously voted him in to become a committer. Nicolas was voted an Apache committer on the 1st of August, 2005. I had several discussions with Nicolas about this new role and he was extremely happy to be part of the Apache Foundation. Nicolas, we'll miss you, but the work you have done for the community will be remembered forever and will live on. Conflict-affected regions in the north are among the hardest hit. A few weeks ago, Priscilla travelled to Dikwa in northeastern Nigeria, where she witnessed first-hand the combined impact of hunger, conflict, economic hardship and climate change. This is her account. Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Humanitarian workers like me and my colleagues cannot reach Dikwa by road. It is simply too dangerous. pages.text: Nike faces religious ban in Libya because it was named after Greek goddess Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes 3 November 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Basma El Atti AFP via Getty Images Nike clothes are popular in Libya, although many are counterfeit Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo. The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings. It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god. Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name. The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country. It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza. A panel of five judges chose the entry, painted in oil, from among 58 best-of-show entries representing U.S. states and territories. “The Junior Duck Stamp Program is one of the Service’s hallmark efforts that helps youth learn about wetlands and waterfowl conservation and foster a lifelong connection with the outdoors. This program supports President Donald J. Trump’s priority to invest directly in youth and future career opportunities through learning,” said Service Director Brian Nesvik

Her reports air regularly on NPR's critically acclaimed newsmagazines All Things Considered , Morning Edition , and Weekend Edition . Totenberg's coverage of the Supreme Court and legal affairs has won her widespread recognition. She is often featured in documentaries — most recently RBG — that deal with issues before the court. As Newsweek put it, "The mainstays [of NPR] are Morning Edition and All Things Considered . But the creme de la creme is Nina Totenberg." In 1991, her ground-breaking report about University of Oklahoma Law Professor Anita Hill's allegations of sexual harassment by Judge Clarence Thomas led the Senate Judiciary Committee to re-open Thomas's Supreme Court confirmation hearings to consider Hill's charges. NPR received the prestigious George Foster Peabody Award for its gavel-to-gavel coverage — anchored by Totenberg — of both the original hearings and the inquiry into Anita Hill's allegations, and for Totenberg's reports and exclusive interview with Hill. The YouGov polling, commissioned by MSI Reproductive Choices to mark its 50th anniversary, found nine in 10 people support the right to access an abortion. This was the case with 94% of Labour voters, 91% of Conservative voters, 95% of Green voters and 86% of Reform voters, pointing to one of the clearest indicators of cross-party political consensus in the UK.
